newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: News says to sell Arizona uplink facility.
newsitem.headline: News says to sell Arizona uplink facility.

text.p: News Corp Ltd said it would sell ASkyB's U.S. satellite uplink facility in Arizona to Tele-Communications Inc as part of its wider deal with satellite TV service PrimeStar Partners.
News Ltd said in its announcement in New York on Wednesday that the facility would be sold for a price representing ASkyB's investment, plus related interest expense.
The advanced satellite and data uplink facility was reported to be a US$130 million project when Gilbert, Arizona, was chosen as the site for the centre in June 1996.
Construction of the building was expected to be completed by the end of June, and the facility was expected to be operating by late 1997 or early 1998, according to Arizona media reports.
ASkyB is owned 80 percent by News and 20 percent by MCI Corp.
News said ASkyB would sell two satellites to PrimeStar in exchange for a non-voting stake in the satellite TV service worth about US$1.1 billion.
Tele-Communications Inc is one of the six owners of PrimeStar.
News Corp also announced on Wednesday that ASkyB would independently sell two additional satellites which are under construction.
